summary: This standard covers companies that mine coal, underground or surface, thermal or metallurgical, and those that make coal products. It addresses greenhouse gas emissions, water and waste (including tailings), biodiversity, indigenous and community relations, labour and worker safety, and how climate regulation affects reserve valuation and capital spending.

questions.text: What is your organisation's gross global Scope 1 greenhouse gas emissions, and what percentage of them is covered under emissions-limiting regulations?
questions.hint: Unit: Metric tonnes (t) CO₂-e, Percentage (%) · Report gross global Scope 1 emissions in metric tonnes CO2-e and, separately, the percentage covered under emissions-limiting regulations (e.g. cap-and-trade or carbon tax schemes).

questions.text: What is your long- and short-term strategy or plan to manage Scope 1 emissions, what are your emissions reduction targets, and how have you performed against them?
questions.hint: Unit: discussion, no unit · Describe the strategy or plan, the targets (scope, baseline year, target year), and an analysis of performance against those targets, including any activities or investments driving the change.

questions.text: What are your organisation's (1) total water withdrawn and (2) total water consumed, and what percentage of each is in regions with High or Extremely High Baseline Water Stress?
questions.hint: Unit: Thousand cubic metres (m³), Percentage (%) · Report (1) total water withdrawn and (2) total water consumed in thousand cubic metres, and the percentage of each in regions with High or Extremely High Baseline Water Stress (e.g. per the WRI Aqueduct tool).

questions.text: How many incidents of non-compliance with water quality permits, standards and regulations did your organisation have?
questions.hint: Unit: Number · Report the total number of incidents of non-compliance with water quality permits, standards and regulations in the reporting period.

questions.text: What is the total weight of non-mineral waste your organisation generated?
questions.hint: Unit: Metric tonnes (t) · Report the total weight of non-mineral waste generated in metric tonnes for the reporting period.

questions.text: What is the total weight of tailings your organisation produced?
questions.hint: Unit: Metric tonnes (t) · Report the total weight of tailings produced in metric tonnes for the reporting period.

questions.text: What is the total weight of waste rock your organisation generated?
questions.hint: Unit: Metric tonnes (t) · Report the total weight of waste rock generated in metric tonnes for the reporting period.

questions.text: What is the total weight of hazardous waste your organisation generated?
questions.hint: Unit: Metric tonnes (t) · Report the total weight of hazardous waste generated in metric tonnes, using the regulatory definition of hazardous waste in each jurisdiction.

questions.text: What is the total weight of hazardous waste your organisation recycled?
questions.hint: Unit: Metric tonnes (t) · Report the total weight of hazardous waste recycled in metric tonnes for the reporting period.

questions.text: How many significant incidents associated with hazardous waste management did your organisation have?
questions.hint: Unit: Number · Report the number of significant incidents (as defined by regulators or your own criteria) associated with hazardous waste management.

questions.text: What waste management policies and procedures do you have for your active and inactive operations?
questions.hint: Unit: discussion, no unit · Describe the policies and procedures covering waste handling, storage, disposal and closure, for both active and inactive (e.g. closed or legacy) operations.

questions.text: What environmental management policies and practices does your organisation have for its active sites?
questions.hint: Unit: discussion, no unit · Describe the policies and practices (e.g. impact assessments, site management plans, rehabilitation commitments) and how they are applied across active sites, including any certifications or standards used.

questions.text: What percentage of your mine sites have acid rock drainage that is (1) predicted to occur, (2) actively mitigated, and (3) under treatment or remediation?
questions.hint: Unit: Percentage (%) · Report each of the three percentages (1) predicted to occur, (2) actively mitigated, (3) under treatment or remediation, as a share of all mine sites.

questions.text: What percentage of your (1) proved and (2) probable reserves are in or near sites with protected conservation status or endangered species habitat?
questions.hint: Unit: Percentage (%) · Report (1) the percentage of proved reserves and (2) the percentage of probable reserves located in or near protected conservation areas or endangered species habitat, and state how 'near' is defined.

questions.text: What percentage of your (1) proved and (2) probable reserves are in or near indigenous land?
questions.hint: Unit: Percentage (%) · Report (1) the percentage of proved reserves and (2) the percentage of probable reserves in or near indigenous land, and state how 'near' is defined.

questions.text: What engagement processes and due diligence practices do you use to manage indigenous rights?
questions.hint: Unit: discussion, no unit · Describe engagement processes (e.g. free, prior and informed consent), due diligence practices and how indigenous rights risks are identified and managed.

questions.text: What process does your organisation use to manage risks and opportunities associated with community rights and interests?
questions.hint: Unit: discussion, no unit · Describe the process for identifying, engaging on and managing community rights and interests, including grievance mechanisms and how outcomes are tracked.

questions.text: What were (1) the number and (2) the duration of non-technical delays at your operations?
questions.hint: Unit: Number, Days · Report (1) the number of non-technical delays (e.g. protests, blockades, permit or community disputes) and (2) their total duration in days.

questions.text: What percentage of your active workforce is employed under collective agreements?
questions.hint: Unit: Percentage (%) · Report the percentage of the active workforce covered by collective bargaining agreements.

questions.text: What were (1) the number and (2) the duration of strikes and lockouts at your organisation?
questions.hint: Unit: Number, Days · Report (1) the number of strikes and lockouts and (2) their total duration in days; include work stoppages involving the active workforce.

questions.text: What are your (1) all-incidence rate, (2) fatality rate, and (3) near miss frequency rate (NMFR) for (a) direct employees and (b) contract employees?
questions.hint: Unit: Rate · Report each rate separately for (a) direct employees and (b) contract employees, stating the basis used (e.g. per 200,000 or 1,000,000 hours worked).

questions.text: How does your organisation manage accident and safety risks and long-term health and safety risks?
questions.hint: Unit: discussion, no unit · Describe the management of accident and safety risks (e.g. ground control, fires, explosions) and long-term health risks (e.g. dust, black lung), including controls, monitoring and training.

questions.text: How sensitive are your coal reserve levels to future price projection scenarios that account for a price on carbon emissions?
questions.hint: Unit: Million metric tonnes (Mt) · Describe the scenarios and price assumptions used and report the resulting change in reserve levels in the unit given.

questions.text: What is the estimated carbon dioxide emissions embedded in your proven coal reserves?
questions.hint: Unit: Metric tonnes (t) CO₂-e · Report the estimated CO2 emissions embedded in proven coal reserves in metric tonnes CO2-e, and state the calculation method and emission factors used.

questions.text: How do price and demand for coal or climate regulation influence your capital expenditure strategy for exploration, acquisition and development of assets?
questions.hint: Unit: discussion, no unit · Describe how price outlooks, demand trends and climate regulation shape capital allocation, including any scenario analysis and asset decisions.

questions.text: Can you provide an inventory table of your tailings storage facilities, with the twelve required fields for each facility from (1) facility name to (12) site-specific EPRP?
questions.hint: Unit: Various · One row per facility: name, location, ownership status, operational status, construction method, maximum permitted storage capacity, tailings currently stored, consequence classification, date of latest independent technical review, material findings, mitigation measures, site-specific EPRP.

questions.text: What tailings management systems and governance structure do you use to monitor and maintain the stability of your tailings storage facilities?
questions.hint: Unit: discussion, no unit · Summarise the management systems, accountable roles, independent reviews, monitoring and the standards followed to maintain tailings storage facility stability.

questions.text: What is your approach to developing Emergency Preparedness and Response Plans (EPRPs) for your tailings storage facilities?
questions.hint: Unit: discussion, no unit · Describe how EPRPs are developed (e.g. dam-break analysis, affected-community involvement), tested, reviewed and updated for each tailings storage facility.

questions.text: What was your organisation's production of thermal coal?
questions.hint: Unit: Million metric tonnes (Mt) · Report production of thermal coal in million metric tonnes for the reporting period.

questions.text: What was your organisation's production of metallurgical coal?
questions.hint: Unit: Million metric tonnes (Mt) · Report production of metallurgical coal in million metric tonnes for the reporting period.
